subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw add a focused `groupScope` main-session option for selected group/channel peers now, or defer this to the broader shared-session routing design?
rationale: This adds new config surface and intentionally changes a session/security boundary, which repository policy treats as maintainer product and security direction even though the source gap is clear.

options.title: Review and narrow the linked PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91702 as the candidate, requiring explicit opt-in semantics, security docs, upgrade/default proof, and conflict resolution before merge.

options.title: Defer to broader shared sessions
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929 canonical if maintainers want named/shared session groups instead of a focused group-to-main option.

options.title: Reject core group-to-main scope
options.body: Keep group/channel sessions isolated in core and document memory or manual context-sharing alternatives for trusted groups.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow the linked PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91702 as the candidate, requiring explicit opt-in semantics, security docs, upgrade/default proof, and conflict resolution before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing and docs history points to this person for the cross-cutting product/security routing decision.
